items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: Karl Berger said something that just made me pause.

ctx.x: No, no not really. And to me it was all about playing with other people and exploring I say this and therefore you say that so therefore I say this. It’s just following natural logic. Now in fact I feel like when I play things without a form I actually sound more inside than when I play on set forms. Because I’m really using my ears and making music with another person like often, yeah, it sounds more inside than outside when I’m not using a set form. Does that make sense?
It does. Karl Berger said something that just made me pause. He said playing free requires much more organization and thought. And like wow I’d never thought of that.

And I completely agree with that. You know I completely agree with that. And playing a lot of that way made me so much more freer when I’m playing over form. And I would also add that doing a lot of different time signatures, like my favorite time signature is seven. And I don’t know I just do games with myself. There was a time where I could pretty much sing or play every bebop head in seven. And I would learn tunes that I felt I needed to learn but I didn’t really want to learn but I’d learn it in seven just to…
